rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Teach principle + technique — default
rules_evaluated.evidence: L43: "The retro you just ran was the compound step of his loop: ideate → brainstorm → plan → work → review → polish → compound → repeat. That is the orient, fix, compound, close loop cut at more joints; same shape, more names." Re-fired after commit 426ebcd reworded the equivalence clause (was "the names differ, the loop doesn't"). Checked the full body for any other use of ideate/brainstorm/plan/work/review/polish/repeat — none appear anywhere else in the file. None of the 7 non-compound stage names are invoked as something the student does, reads a prompt for, or is asked to apply; only `compound` is tied to an action ("The retro you just ran was the compound step"), and it is anchored. The 7 exist solely to place the lived step inside Klaassen's named sequence.
rules_evaluated.judge_note: Re-derived, not carried forward. Two questions on re-fire: (1) does 426ebcd's 'same shape, more names' change the cognitive-load picture? Yes — net improvement, and independently of the 2026-08-02 amendment. The pre-amendment REVISE this chain traces to wasn't about noun-count; it was that the closer asked the student to accept unqualified loop-equivalence across a visibly doubled step count ('the names differ, the loop doesn't' implied same cardinality, different labels only). That's a real Understand-level mental-model risk — a student who can count sees 4 vs 8 stages and has to silently reconcile a gap the old text denied existed. 'Same shape, more names' removes that reconciliation burden by naming the count difference instead of eliding it; the claim now matches what's printed on the page two clauses earlier. This is a pedagogy-owned fix (LO-accuracy / mental-model formation at this Bloom level), not merely a backing citation patch, and it reinforces PASS on a second, independent ground alongside the amended orientation/invocation test — two separate reasons converging, not one carrying the other. (2) Does the routing of 'seven lexical items in one sentence' to check_writing.md still hold, checked fresh rather than deferred? Yes. This edit changes zero words in the stage list itself — same 7 names, same sentence — so if in-sentence density were a pedagogy violation, this edit would not have moved it either way. Re-scanned check_pedagogy.md for any rule reaching sentence-level lexical load independent of the invocation test: §57's 'per-moment cognitive load stays single-task' is scoped to new-mechanic packaging (tools/sessions), not naming density in an orientation sentence; §14 itself states 'counting unexplained nouns is the wrong test.' No other numbered rule reaches sentence-craft. The routing is correct on independent re-check, not because a predecessor already wrote it down — density/chunking is check_writing.md's register territory when nothing in the sentence is being invoked.
